tasks.short: Notify colleagues of defects and direct adjustment work

steps.what: Notify workers of defects and clarify required adjustments to extruding and forming machines

tasks.design: Retain direct defect communication and clarification with the operator. Recording the defect is handled separately; no duplicate communication saving is claimed from a fault log.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workers need shared understanding of the observed problem and the machine context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing direct communication supports immediate clarification.
tasks.still_hard: Communicating uncertainty and avoiding inappropriate adjustment instructions.
tasks.human_edge: The operator confirms that colleagues understand the concern and can raise questions.

reach.learn: Describe symptoms without presenting a guess as a confirmed cause

evidence.claim: Manual defect coordination is an E1 proposal; the textile dashboard digest does not establish replacement of adjustment discussions.

assumptions: The baseline is live communication rather than writing a malfunction record.
The operator obtains defect observations through separate equipment observation and explains them within s1; all communication time remains counted.
No machine consumes a structured defect cause or adjustment-authority flag.
Existing communication suffices; no new service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Which misunderstandings cause repeated defect clarification?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; gross and net saving zero. Fault-record preparation savings belong to the separate record task.

tasks.short: Observe machine operations and gauges for malfunction signs

steps.what: Observe machine operations, control boards and gauges to detect signs of malfunctions

tasks.design: Retain direct machine and gauge observation with the operator. Existing indications support the work; no unvalidated classifier replaces recognition of clogged components or faulty applicators.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment faults depend on local behaviour and operating conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing gauges and control boards provide indications for direct interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Recognizing early symptoms and separating normal variation from a fault.
tasks.human_edge: The operator combines visual and instrument evidence and seeks inspection when unsure.

reach.learn: Relate observed symptoms to the operating context

evidence.claim: Human monitoring is an E1 proposal; a production dashboard does not establish validated detection of these fiber-machine faults.

assumptions: This baseline covers observing equipment, excluding notifications and record preparation assigned separately.
The operator observes readings and behaviour during s1 with all time retained; no free diagnosed-fault input is assumed.
No new monitoring service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Which observed fault modes have validated instrument alarms on the actual equipment?

already_counted.description: Observe readings and machine behaviour and interpret concerns

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving. No validated physical monitoring replacement is supplied.

steps.what: Capture machine malfunctions with dated observations and source references
Populate malfunction record templates from captured details without repeated transcription
Check malfunction details, resolve missing fields and save the record

tasks.design: Configure one capture form and native record templates in {OPS_SYSTEM}, removing a second transcription into the shift record. The operator supplies symptoms and checks the record; the system neither diagnoses the fault nor directs adjustment work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated copying from a local note into a central malfunction record.
tasks.enabler_now: A shared records form can reuse captured fields directly.
tasks.still_hard: Describing ambiguous symptoms and preserving what is unknown about the cause.
tasks.human_edge: The operator distinguishes observed symptoms from a confirmed maintenance finding.

reach.learn: Record symptoms in a form that supports later investigation

evidence.claim: Valia Furniture exposes production and maintenance data on dashboards; this supports a broad records capability analogy, not a measured fiber-machine logging saving.
The proposed single-capture fault form and savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: Saving concerns repeated transcription only; physical fault detection and colleague notification are excluded.

The operator produces machine identifier, timestamp, observed symptom, job reference and optional supporting indication in s1; 40 hours include all capture. Unknown cause stays unknown; missing fields are handled manually in s3.
Native OPS_SYSTEM forms precede custom integration or a language model.
The hypothesis requires an existing second copy; if there is only one entry, no transcription saving exists.
research_questions: Does one checked form replace a real second transcription while preserving symptom detail?

already_counted.description: Symptom capture and final record checks

incremental.description: Maintain fields and audit missing or misleading records

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=70 yields 30 gross less 7 focal upkeep =23 central net. Report 0-4 until duplicate transcription is observed; the low case already enters once.

tasks.short: Prepare and attach operational machine tags

steps.what: Capture operational data and verify the intended machine and tag purpose
Format and print operational tags from the captured fields
Check printed tags and attach each tag to the correct machine

tasks.design: Configure native label templates and printing in {OPS_SYSTEM} after the operator captures and verifies operational fields. Retain legibility checks, machine matching and physical tag attachment with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manually laying out and writing the same fields on routine operational tags.
tasks.enabler_now: Native label printing can format captured values without interpreting machine condition.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong-machine attachment and tags that become unreadable in the operating environment.
tasks.human_edge: The operator checks the physical machine and tag at the point of attachment.

reach.learn: Make tag purpose and version visible

evidence.claim: Native printing of structured operational tags is a proposed E1 configuration; the digest does not document this fiber-machine deployment.

assumptions: These are routine operational tags, not safety isolation or release permits; physical attachment is never automated.

In s1 the operator produces machine identifier, job identifier, observation date, required reading values and tag purpose; 35 hours include capture and correction. Missing or uncertain values require manual resolution before printing.
Native OPS_SYSTEM label templates precede custom software.
Malfunction narratives belong to the separate fault-record task; no capture or saving is shared or counted twice.
research_questions: Can printed tags remain readable and correctly matched while reducing actual handwriting time?

already_counted.description: Operational field capture, tag check and physical attachment

incremental.description: Maintain tag templates, stock and print checks
Support printer connection and template integrity
